parts: I have no idea what the person means when he says "try different starting values", or "make sure that the variances of your variables are within an order of magnitude of one another".

You can see how to set starting values on the ?model.syntax help page, but I don't think that should be necessary.  You have 3 predictors whose variances are notably larger than the rest (appearance, weight, and physical).  You could create a copy of your data and divide each of those variables by 10, then run your model on that copy.  The slopes would be interpreted as change in the outcome per 10 units of those predictors, rather than per 1-unit change in those predictors.
